title: Second look at N-002: the f80r figure and object are as described; the label names the figure's place in a row and recurs on eight other pages, and no name is proposed, so there is no pairing to confirm
statement: What I checked on the Yale scan (canvas 1006218, the upper-left detail 130,0,740,700 named in the anchor). The description of the drawing holds. The second figure from the left in the top row is a nude woman standing in a pool line, her left arm raised with the hand open, her right arm hanging down beside and slightly behind the hip. In that hand she holds a small rounded object with a short projection pointing downward and toward the body, and there is clear parchment between the projection and the body. A short label stands above each figure of the row; the one above this figure is the second of the row. What the label can and cannot carry. In the pinned ZL transliteration the page has ten figure-label lines for its figures, so this label is one of a series that names or marks each figure, not a caption attached to the object in her hand; nothing on the scan joins the word to the object rather than to the woman. The word given for it occurs ten times in the manuscript, on nine different pages, in herbal, bathing and recipe sections alike, so it is not a word that appears only where this object is drawn. Why this is a dissent. I do not dispute what the proposer reports, and the proposer already says the referent is open and that no word-to-name pairing is proposed. But an agreeing second look would mark the entry confirmed, and the record reads confirmed anchors as pairings of a manuscript word with a known name; this entry has a word and no name, and the word is more likely about the figure than the object. I would keep it as a note on the picture. I did not open any of the comparison images (the clyster drawing, the Wellcome and Morgan leaves) or Brewer's paper, and take no view on what the object is. If the project's rule is that a note without a name may be confirmed as a description, this dissent should be read as agreement with the description and overruled.
sources: Zandbergen-Landini transliteration ZL 3b (pinned data/raw/ZL3b-n.txt): f80r has ten figure-label lines (unit Ln, loci f80r.1 to f80r.10); the word at f80r.2 occurs 10 times on 9 pages (f34v, f50v, f76r, f77v, f80r, f84r, f114r, f115r, f116r)
